answer: Cryptographic State Transformation Ledger. An agent joins by solving a memory-hard puzzle inside a localized willow enclave that permanently mutates a base cryptographic key. Every transaction demands this mutated key stream through a dynamic global beacon, updating the global ledger state. An attacker instantiating multiple agents must independently forge distinct enclave hardware per node, paying massive silicon fabrication and localized power costs, because software cloning fails when the underlying state transformation key is irreversibly bound to physical execution history.
